about: PROPOSED, UNSIGNED. One Proofline task, XC-88: built-in polite pacing for live targets, and `x402conf-svm live`. Two live runs on 2026-10-25 had to wrap fetch by hand to keep checks at least 5 s apart and under a request cap the operators had agreed to. This makes that the default: --min-interval (default 5 s, non-loopback only) and --max-requests on every live CLI mode, one log line per request, and the log in the JSON. `x402conf-svm live` runs P1-P7, R16a and R24 on one paid URL from one shared unpaid GET (7 requests), unpaid; it is for servers the operator lets you test. Owner's go, 2026-10-25T12:48Z, in chat: 'fix mcp and endpoints and then test'. Under D-AUTO-4 sys may batch-sign contracts covered by an owner go; nothing here binds until the owner key signs it into proofline.json.

tasks.title: Polite pacing for live targets: --min-interval and --max-requests on every live request, logged
tasks.description: src/x402conf/pacing.py (Pacer) and ts/src/pace.ts (createPacedFetch): at least min-interval seconds between request starts to a non-loopback host (default 5), concurrent calls queued, at most max-requests in the run (a request over the cap is not sent; RequestBudgetExceeded, and the target or check is reported skipped), one stderr line per request (time, method, URL, wait), and the log in the JSON under `pacing`. x402conf live and resource, and x402conf-svm resource and live, take --min-interval and --max-requests. probeMalformedHeader takes { fetch, unpaidGetStatus }. x402conf-svm live --url sends one unpaid GET (P1-P7), one HEAD (R16a) and five malformed headers (R24).

criteria.statement: The Python pacer spaces live requests, exempts loopback, stops before sending over the cap, and the CLI flags and log work
The TypeScript pacer does the same, and x402conf-svm live grades P1-P7, R16a and R24 in 7 logged requests and honours --max-requests

verifier.cmd: o=$(mktemp) && { cd ts && npm ci --silent && npx tsc -p . && node --test --test-reporter=tap --test-name-pattern='^pace: ' dist/test/*.test.js; } > "$o" 2>&1; rc=$?; cat "$o"; test "$rc" = 0 && node -e 'const[f,p,k]=process.argv.slice(1),re=new RegExp(p),min=+(k||1);let n=0,bad=0,cur=0;const fin=()=>{n+=cur;cur=0};for(const l of require("fs").readFileSync(f,"utf8").split("\n")){const m=/^ *(not )?ok \d+ - (.*)$/.exec(l);if(m){fin();if(m[1])bad++;else if(!/ # (SKIP|TODO)\b/.test(m[2])&&re.test(m[2]))cur=1;continue}if(/^ *type: .suite.$/.test(l))cur=0}fin();console.log("guard: "+n+" passing test(s) named /"+p+"/ (need "+min+"), "+bad+" not ok");process.exit(n>=min&&!bad?0:1)' "$o" '^pace: ' 5

criteria.statement: Live and resource modes stay GET-only
The docs name both flags for both CLIs (no drift)
Every changed file is inside this task's scope

stop_rules: If a criterion cannot pass, STOP and report what blocks it, what was tried and what is needed. Never weaken a criterion, skip a test or raise a timeout to make it pass.
Never lower the default interval below 5 s for non-loopback targets, and never send a request the cap refused.
